title: Watch: stronger eastern border regions through cooperation
content:
A new documentary follows Europe’s eastern border regions as they turn shared geopolitical challenges into practical ideas, stronger partnerships and more resilient communities through interregional cooperation.

How can regions respond when long-standing cross-border links are disrupted by war, closed borders and growing security concerns? 

The 12-minute documentary ‘Stronger eastern border regions: the Regio-Silience’ journey follows two years of collaboration among more than 30 local and regional authorities from Poland, the Baltic States, Finland and Norway. 

Supported by the Interreg Europe Policy Learning Platform, Regio-Silience brings regions together to exchange experience and explore practical responses in economic development, security, community resilience and regional cooperation. The film shows the journey from Antwerp to policy-learning activities in Olsztyn, Salla and Kirkenes. 

The documentary also shows how regional experience can inform the European debate on the future of the EU’s eastern border regions. It highlights the value of peer learning and cooperation in developing practical ideas, building lasting partnerships and strengthening resilience.

title: Building bridges to adulthood: PA Education shares School to Work experience in Brussels
content:
How can local and regional actors provide more coordinated support to vulnerable young people as they move into adulthood? This question was at the centre of a workshop held on 14 October 2026 during the European Week of Regions and Cities in Brussels.

The workshop, No child left behind: building bridges to adulthood, was organised by the European Commission, Directorate-General for Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion (DG EMPL), together with Eurocities. Around 50 participants gathered to discuss how young people can receive more continuous and coordinated support when transitioning between education, employment and social services.

Anders Bergström, Policy Area Coordinator for Education under the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR), participated as a panellist, sharing experiences from the flagship School to Work (S2W).

title: Youth Democracy Festivals empower youth as the future of democracy
content:
Through D-Effect project, young people across the Baltic Sea Region co-create Youth Democracy Festivals, strengthening civic participation, democratic skills and cooperation between youth and decision-makers.

Young people are often invited to discuss democracy, but rarely have a real opportunity to shape it. The Interreg South Baltic project D-Effect is changing this approach by giving youth an active role in designing and delivering democratic initiatives within their communities.

Implemented by partners from Poland, Sweden, Denmark, Germany and Lithuania, D-Effect promotes civic engagement through a practical methodology built around Round Tables, Youth Democracy Festivals (YDF) and direct dialogue with decision-makers. Rather than being passive participants, young people become co-creators of activities that address local challenges and strengthen democratic culture.

title: Three new EU funded projects – one shared mission: Boosting Rural Circular Bioeconomy
content:
In autumn 2026, three Interreg Baltic Sea Region projects – CircularFarmPlastics, Rural Symbiosis and BioGold – are launching with a shared mission: to boost circular bioeconomy in rural areas by turning side streams, residues and difficult waste streams into new value, stronger cooperation and practical business opportunities.

The BioBoosters Network is hosting an open launch webinar for three projects advancing the rural circular bioeconomy in the Baltic Sea Region: BioGold, CircularFarmPlastics and Rural Symbiosis. The event will introduce their activities and explore opportunities for cooperation with the project teams. The webinar is particularly relevant to farmers, biogas producers, rural businesses, waste collection and recycling companies, regional and local authorities, researchers, and business support organisations interested in practical circular bioeconomy solutions.

title: Cities turning climate ambition into action: Climate Budget Summit
content:
The Climate Budget Summit at the EU Regions Week in Brussels brought city leaders, climate experts, and local practitioners to explore how municipalities can turn ambitious climate goals into concrete investments and measurable actions.

The Summit on 14 October 2026 was launched by the Climate-4-CAST project (co-funded by the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme and contributing to thw EUSBSR Policy Area Energy Actions) to emphasise the role of climate budgeting in helping cities align their financial decisions with climate neutrality objectives.

Organised as a partner event of the EU Week of Regions and Cities, it hosted ca. 50 participants sharing experiences and reflecting on practical solutions for including climate considerations in budgeting and governance. The discussion touched upon common challenges, such as how to manage competing priorities, limited resources and political realities. Most participants represented European local and regional authorities, alongside representatives from the European Commission’s DG REGIO, the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme, and the city networks Eurocities, ICLEI and UBC.

title: BSR Cultural Pearls 2027: Applications Submitted, Cultural Pearls 2027 will be announced on 9 November
content:
The applications for BSR Cultural Pearls 2027 have been submitted, and the jury has begun its evaluation. The title recipients will be announced on 9 November 2026. Meanwhile, Cultural Pearls cities continue to bring communities together through cultural activities.

The past weeks have marked an important stage for BSR Cultural Pearls. Applications for the 2027 title have been submitted, and the international jury, comprising 11 members, has started evaluating the submitted Community Resilience Action Plans (CuReAPs). The applications reflect the participating municipalities’ approaches to addressing local challenges, strengthening community resilience and using culture to encourage citizen participation.

The new BSR Cultural Pearl will be announced on 9 November 2026, marking the next milestone in the programme. The selected municipality will join a growing network of towns and cities across the Baltic Sea Region that use culture as a means of fostering community engagement, dialogue and a sense of belonging.

An award ceremony is planned for 17 November in Glücksburg, as part of the first Future Cities Forum (16–18 November 2026).

title: 9th MSP Planners’ Forum meeting explores nature restoration in maritime spatial planning
content:
Yesterday, on 22 October, VASAB and EUSBSR PA Spatial Planning hosted the 9th MSP Planners’ Forum meeting online, focusing on nature restoration and its integration into maritime spatial planning (MSP).

As always, the MSP Planners’ Forum brought together maritime spatial planning practitioners from across the Baltic Sea Region to exchange updates on national MSP developments, discuss pressing challenges and share national approaches to this meeting’s main topic – nature restoration.

title: Norway’s EUSBSR accession opens new opportunities for cooperation in education and social inclusion
content:
Norway’s full participation in the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) was officially celebrated in Oslo on 16 October 2026. For Policy Area Education, the occasion was also an opportunity to strengthen dialogue with Norwegian stakeholders and explore new possibilities for cooperation on shared societal challenges.

Norway became the ninth participating country in the EUSBSR on 18 May 2026, marking an important step in strengthening cooperation across the Baltic Sea Region.

The official launch event in Oslo on 16 October brought together Norwegian Minister of Foreign Affairs Espen Barth Eide, Minister of Local Government and Regional Development Bjørnar Skjæran, representatives of the European Commission, Policy Area Coordinators and stakeholders from across the region.

The programme focused on Norway’s role in the Strategy, its longstanding experience of Baltic Sea cooperation and the opportunities that full participation creates for contributing to shared priorities.

title: Cohesion builds the precondition for a competitive Europe and the Baltic Sea Region
content:
The Baltic Sea Region, like all macro-regions, faces challenges that no country, region or city can tackle alone. Resilience, competitiveness, climate work and connectivity all require territorial solutions. This was the starting point for the session “Fit for purpose – EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region builds a competitive, prosperous and carbon neutral region” at the EU Week of Regions and Cities 2026.

The EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region Action Plan (2026, pending Commission approval) gave the framework for the discussion. The recently updated Action Plan is the most geographically and thematically comprehensive framework for transnational work in the Baltic Sea Region. The Member States of the Strategy highlight the urgent need to respond to challenges such as a rapidly evolving security environment and increasingly complex multi-hazard risks: accelerating climate change and persistent environmental pressures, demographic change, and the demands of the green and digital transitions.

title: Nautical Mail – Policy Area Ship Newsletter
content:
O-HOY and Welcome Dear Reader,

Enjoy the pleasure of viewing the latest Newsletter by the EU Strategy of the Baltic Sea Region Policy Area for Sustainable Shipping (SHIP)!

PA Ship News

Coordination of the PA Ship is changing. Finnish Transport and Communications Agency will pass over the role of the Policy Area Coordination to Kotka Maritime Research Center Merikotka from 1st of January 2027 onwards. Coordinators from Traficom will pass over all material and knowledge forward to the coordinators at Merikotka. We wish all the best and smooth sails to the new coordinators!

SAVING THE SEA – News from our Projects

Circular Ports

Circular Ports has had an active start to autumn! The project has been represented at several events around the Baltic Sea Region, while work continues with all six pilots.

In August, Circular Ports took part in the Europe Forum in Turku with the Harbours of Change: Circular Economy in Baltic Sea Ports session, bringing together perspectives from EUSBSR PA Ship, Port of Turku and Circular Ports pilots on practical circular economy solutions in port environments. Read more about the session and its key takeaways here.
